questions.question: A solid weighs 4.8g in air, 2.8g in water and 3.2g in Kerosine. The ratio of density of the solid to that of the kerosine is
questions.explanation: Upthrust in water = 4.8-2.8=2.0 g; in kerosine = 4.8-3.2=1.6 g. RD of solid = 4.8/2.0=2.4; RD of kerosine = 1.6/2.0=0.8; ratio = 2.4/0.8 = 3. So D.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: One of the following readings represents the measurement of the length of a metal rod using vernier calipers. Taking the reading accuracy into consideration, the most likely one is
questions.explanation: Vernier calipers typically read to 0.01 cm, so 5.16 cm is appropriate.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: When a sound wave passes from air into water its
options: speed and frequency increases but its wavelength remains the same
speed and wavelength increases but its frequency remains the same
speed increases but its frequency and wavelength decreases
questions.explanation: Frequency remains constant; speed increases in water, so wavelength increases.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: A convex mirror is used as a driving mirror because I. its image is erect II. It has a large field of view III. It has a long focal length. Identify the CORRECT statement(s)
questions.explanation: Convex mirrors give erect images and a wide field of view; long focal length is not the primary reason.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: A magnetic needle is suspended first at the earth's north magnetic pole and then at a point on the magnetic equator. The respective angles between the needle and the horizontal are
questions.explanation: At magnetic poles, dip = 90°; at equator, dip = 0°.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: A hydrometer is an instrument for measuring the
options: depth of water in a vessel
relative density of a liquid by the method of flotation
relative density of a liquid by finding the apparent loss in weight
questions.explanation: A hydrometer measures relative density based on buoyancy.

questions.question: The refractive index of a liquid is 1.5. If the velocity of light in vacuum is 3.0 × 10⁸ ms⁻¹, the velocity of light in the liquid is

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: A ship travelling towards a cliff receives the echo of its whistle after 3.5 seconds. A short while later, it receives the echo after 2.5 seconds. If the speed of sound in air under the prevailing condition is 250 ms⁻¹, how much closer is the ship to the cliff?
questions.explanation: Distance in first case = 250×3.5/2 = 437.5 m; second = 250×2.5/2 = 312.5 m; difference = 125 m.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: Which of the following statements about defects of vision is/are CORRECT? I. For a long sighted person, close objects appear blurred II. For a short sighted person, distant objects appear blurred III. Short sight is corrected by using a pair of converging lenses
questions.explanation: Long sight (hypermetropia) → close objects blurred (I). Short sight (myopia) → distant objects blurred (II). Short sight is corrected with diverging lenses, not converging (III false).

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: Which of the following conditions are necessary and sufficient for total internal reflection to take place at the boundary between two optical media? I. Light is passing from optical denser medium to optically less dense medium II. Light is passing from optically less dense medium to optically denser medium III. Angle of incidence is greater than a certain critical value IV. Angle of incidence is lesser than a certain critical value
questions.explanation: Total internal reflection requires denser to rarer (I) and angle of incidence > critical angle (III).

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: The linear expansivity of brass is 2 × 10⁻⁵ °C⁻¹. If the volume of piece of brass is 10 cm³ at 0°C, what will be its volume at 100°C?
questions.explanation: γ = 3α = 6e-5. ΔV = γVΔT = 6e-5 × 10 × 100 = 0.06 cm³. New volume = 10.06 cm³.

questions.question: The lower and upper fixed points marked on a Mercury-in-glass thermometer are 210 mm apart. The end of the mercury column in the tube is 49 mm above the lower fixed point in a room. What is the temperature of the room in degrees Celsius?

questions.question: Which of the following instruments consumes the highest current? I. Electric iron 250V 1kW II. Television set 220V 110W III. Torchlight 6V 30W IV. Immersion heater 110V 500W

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: Which of the following pairs is part of the electromagnetic spectrum? I. Radio waves II. sound waves III. Gamma rays IV. water waves
questions.explanation: Radio waves and gamma rays are electromagnetic; sound and water are mechanical.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: A substance has half-life of 3 min. After 6 min, the count rate was observed to be 400. What was its count rate at zero time?
questions.explanation: 6 min = 2 half-lives. Initial count = 400 × 2² = 400×4 = 1600.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: An electric generator with a power output of 3.0KW at a voltage of 1.5KV distributes power along cables of resistance 20.0Ω. The power loss in the cables is
questions.explanation: Current I = P/V = 3000/1500 = 2 A. Power loss = I²R = 4×20 = 80 W.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: In a pure semiconductor, the number of electrons in the conduction band is
options: less than the number of holes in the valence band
equal to the number of holes in the valence band
greater than the number of holes in the valence band
twice the number of holes in the valence band
questions.explanation: In intrinsic semiconductors, electron and hole concentrations are equal.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: A projection lantern is used to give the image of a slide on a screen. If the image is 24 times as large as the slide and the screen is 72.0m from the projecting lens, what is the position of the slide from the lens?
questions.explanation: Magnification m = v/u = 24, v = 72 m, so u = v/m = 72/24 = 3.0 m.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: A thin wire with heavy weights attached to both ends is hung over a block of ice resting on two supports. If the wire cuts through the ice block while the block remains solid behind the wire, the process is called
questions.explanation: Regelation is the process where ice melts under pressure and refreezes when pressure is removed.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: One end of a long wire is fixed while a vibrator is attached to the other end. When the vibrator is energized, the types of waves generated in the wire are
questions.explanation: Waves in a stretched string are transverse and become stationary due to reflection.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: Light of energy 5eV falls on a metal of work function 3eV and electrons are liberated. The stopping potential is
questions.explanation: Maximum kinetic energy = photon energy - work function = 5 - 3 = 2 eV, so stopping potential = 2V.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: What optical instrument can best be constructed with converging lenses of focal lengths 50cm and 5cm?
questions.explanation: An astronomical telescope uses a long focal length objective and short focal length eyepiece (both converging lenses).

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: If the fraction of the atoms of a radioactive material left after 120years is 1/64, what is the half-life of the material?
questions.explanation: 1/64 = (1/2)^6 → 6 half-lives = 120 years → half-life = 20 years.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: If the force and the velocity on a system are each reduced simultaneously by half, the power of the system is
questions.explanation: Power P = Fv. If both halved, P' = (F/2)(v/2) = Fv/4 = P/4.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.topic: Properties of Matter - Density of Water
questions.question: A quantity of water at 0°C is heated to about 30°C. At each degree rise in temperature, its density will
questions.explanation: Water has maximum density at 4°C; from 0°C to 4°C density increases, then decreases.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: An engineer intends to deviate a light ray from its path by 120° through reflection from a plane mirror. Calculate the angle of incidence
questions.explanation: Deviation = 180° - 2i. Given deviation 120°, 120 = 180 - 2i → 2i = 60 → i = 30°.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: I. Its velocity is constant II. No work is done on the body III. It has constant acceleration directed away from the centre IV. The centripetal force is directed towards the centre. Which combination of the above is true of a body moving with constant speed in a circular track?
questions.explanation: In uniform circular motion, speed is constant but velocity changes; work done is zero (force perpendicular to motion); centripetal force is towards centre. So II and IV.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: A handbag containing some load weighing 162N is carried by two students each holding the handle of the bag next to him. If each handle is pulled 60° to the vertical, find the force on each student's arm
questions.explanation: Vertical components: 2T cos60° = 162 → 2T×0.5 = 162 → T = 162 N.
